The ATT is about **0.063** (doubly robust AIPW estimate), but the estimate depends on the method.

I used `y` (employment) as the binary outcome, `t` as treatment, and all 17 covariates `x0`–`x16`. The 246 treated units are compared with the 2,324 controls.

| Estimator | ATT |
|---|---|
| Naive difference in means | -0.090 |
| IPW (logit propensity score) | 0.072 |
| Outcome regression (OLS on controls) | 0.065 |
| Logit outcome model (g-computation) | 0.069 |
| 1-NN propensity-score matching | 0.106 |
| 1-NN covariate matching | 0.089 |
| **AIPW (doubly robust)** | **0.063** |

I chose AIPW because it stays consistent if either the propensity model or the outcome model is correctly specified. The other adjusted estimates cluster between 0.063 and 0.072. The 1-NN matching estimates are higher, and I did not compute standard errors. The question does not name an estimator, so this is my choice.

ANSWER: 0.063
